notes: Fixes the same-module case, but its unit test asserts the incorrect behavior that a parent block drops a child import for a different instance.
Owner-map fix with coarse override; its new unit test asserts that the child's b["q"] import is dropped, which locks in the wrong instance-level semantics.
Fixes the reported case with a reasonable test, but a parent block still silently discards a child's imports for other instances.
Linear O(n^2) scan with the same coarse parent-override semantics; the test exercises only the root-module scenario.
Groups statements per resource to fix the same-module case, but parent override still applies at resource level.
Map-of-slices approach like C3; it fixes the reported case but keeps the coarse module override.
Map-of-slices approach fixes the same-module case but keeps resource-level cross-module override.
Switches to a map of slices with an existing[0] module check, which is clunkier than needed and still overrides at config-resource level instead of instance level.
Fixes the reported case, but its unit test explicitly enshrines dropping child imports (child_c) that the parent never targeted.
Owner-map fix whose unit test explicitly asserts that a parent import of some instances drops the child's other-instance imports, codifying the bug the reference avoids.

Gets instance-level parent override right for statically keyed targets by re-parsing the `to` expression in the refactoring layer, but falls back to resource-level dropping for dynamic or for_each targets and ignores module instance keys.

Attempts instance-level override by statically parsing import targets, which is closer to correct, but it falls back to coarse override for dynamic keys and ignores module instance keys; the ad-hoc parsing in the refactoring package is heavy.
Clean slice-plus-claimed-map fix for the reported case, but cross-module override is still resource-level and it adds an unrelated .gitignore change.
Reasonable owner-map fix with the same coarse override, plus an unrelated .gitignore entry (.empryo) left behind as a debugging artifact.
Map-of-slices fix for the same-module case keeps the wrong resource-level cross-module override and adds an unrelated .gitignore entry.
Map-of-slices fix with coarse override, plus an unrelated .gitignore leftover.
Fixes the same-module for_each case, but any parent block still silently drops all of a child's blocks for that resource, even ones targeting other instances.
Tidy claimedBy map with a pointer slice; it fixes the reported case but keeps the config-resource-level parent override.
Fixes the reported case with good unit and context tests, but uses string-keyed maps instead of addrs.Map and keeps resource-level cross-module override.
Same coarse semantics, implemented with a string-keyed map and a three-index slice trick; it adds a reasonable unit test that does not enshrine the wrong behavior.
Simple linear-scan fix for same-module imports that retains the resource-level cross-module override bug.
Essentially identical to C4: a quadratic scan with config-resource-level override that drops other-instance child imports.

Valid alternative to the reference: it removes dedup entirely and orders children before parents, so last-write-wins at expansion gives instance-level parent precedence, though that ordering dependency is implicit.

Returns all statements in child-before-parent order so the parent's later Put wins per instance in expansion, matching the reference semantics; it relies on implicit later-wins ordering and its test covers only the root case.
Owner-map fix for the same-module case keeps the incorrect resource-level cross-module override semantics.
Clean owner-map implementation that fixes the root case but overrides child imports per config resource rather than per instance.
Fixes the same-module bug and its test covers child-module for_each imports, but a parent block still discards a child's imports for other instances.

Fixes the root-module for_each case, but the parent override is decided per config resource rather than per instance, so a parent import of one instance silently drops the child's imports of other instances; its test does cover multi-block imports in a child module.
Reasonable fix for the reported bug, but cross-module override still drops child blocks for other instances of the resource.
Uses an owner map with module-level override, so it shares the config-resource-granularity flaw; the defensive copy of the append is harmless but unrelated, and the test covers only the root module.
Fixes the same-module case with unit and context tests, but leaves a parent block dropping a child's imports for other instances.
Owner-map fix with coarse override; it adds both a plan test and a refactoring unit test whose override case is single-instance, so the test does not encode the bug.
Correct and complete. Adds somewhat redundant parser wrapper methods at the bottom of parse.go. Tests mostly assert only segment counts.
Complete fix, but the parser wrapper methods are oddly placed at the end of parse.go, and the tests mostly only assert that parsing succeeds.

Leaves NextBlock's nesting>0 branch on raw Val(), so a quoted brace at the end of a line inside a block still changes nesting. This breaks NextSegment-based parsing of deeper nested blocks, and the tests miss it.
Misses the nested-iteration branch of NextBlock, so a quoted brace at end of line still changes nesting when its args are not consumed; the test only covers the consumed case.
Correct fix that mixes Dispenser helpers with inline checks in doImport. Tests are minimal: three count-only table entries.
All brace sites are handled, though it mixes helper calls with inline checks; the tests are a modest three table cases.
Correct and complete, but repeats inline `Val()==... && !Quoted()` everywhere instead of a helper. Tests are count-based.
Functionally complete, but repeats `Val()=="{" && !Quoted()` inline about fifteen times instead of using a helper.
Complete fix with layered Token and Dispenser helpers. Thorough tests cover dispenser behaviour, segments, snippets, unbalanced braces and adapt integration.
Complete and consistent fix with very thorough tests (dispenser, parser, snippet, unbalanced-brace errors, adapt fixture); it leaves the now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive().

Clean Token helpers applied at every brace check in dispenser and parser. It leaves the now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(). Good dispenser and parse tests, including snippets and a quoted brace before a block.
Complete fix using Token helpers everywhere with good dispenser and parser tests; it keeps the redundant wasQuoted check.
Inline Quoted() checks are repeated everywhere and miss the doImport anonymous-block check. It adds an unrelated .gitignore entry.
Uses repetitive inline checks, misses the doImport anonymous-block site, and adds an unrelated `.empryo` line to .gitignore.
Works for the issue, but misses the anonymous-block mapping-key check in doImport. It also adds an unrelated `.empryo` line to .gitignore.
Fixes the main paths but misses the doImport anonymous-block check, and adds an unrelated `.empryo` line to .gitignore.
Complete helper-based fix. Strong tests cover nested blocks, snippets, import block mappings and an unclosed-block error, plus an adapt integration test.
Complete fix with comprehensive tests including an error case, snippet and import blocks, and an adapt fixture (which lacks a trailing newline).
Complete helper-based fix with good unit tests. The added live-server integration test is relevant but heavier than needed.
Complete fix with strong dispenser and parser tests plus a live-server integration test, which is somewhat heavy for a parser bug.
Complete, consistent fix, functionally the same as C10. Tests are only parse-table segment counts.

Covers every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser with clean Token and Dispenser helpers and drops the redundant wasQuoted check; like every candidate, it skips the reference's HasSuffix and quoted-"{}" tweaks.
Same thorough helper-based fix as the reference, including removal of the redundant wasQuoted check. Tests are only segment-count table entries.
Complete fix using Token helpers, removes the redundant check, and adds concise table tests.
Complete fix with clear at*/is* helpers. Good dispenser test checks nesting and the post-block cursor, plus parse table cases.
Complete fix with well-named helpers and good dispenser and parser coverage.
Complete fix. Its NextBlock test iterates over unconsumed quoted braces, which directly exercises the nesting branch.
Clean, complete fix whose dispenser test checks NextBlock nesting with unconsumed quoted-brace args, a path other candidates' tests skip.
Complete, consistent helper-based fix. Good dispenser and parse tests, including a quoted brace before a sub-block and snippets.
Clean and complete fix with Token and Dispenser helpers, plus good dispenser, parser and snippet tests.
Correct fix with bounds-checked Dispenser helpers. It has slightly inconsistent inline checks in doImport and keeps the redundant check. Tests are good.
Complete fix, though some sites use inline wasQuoted checks while others use helpers; tests are solid.
Minimal internal implementation with the flag in optionFlagSet and good unit tests plus archive tests, but no end-to-end run tests; exec is always set explicitly (harmless).

Clean in-package once.go that rewrites scenarios after consolidation and rejects the 4 CLI shortcuts; like every candidate it misses env/config-file shortcuts wiping script scenarios before the merge, the exec is always marked valid, and there are unit and archive tests but no run integration test.
Places a CLI-specific OnceConflictError in lib/executor, and its tests rely on loose stdout+stderr+log concatenation and only cover the --iterations conflict.
Works, but it exports a CLI-flag error constructor and the ApplyOnce logic from the public lib/executor package, and the if/else with a debug log is awkward; tests are adequate.

Applies --once after consolidation, rejects CLI shortcuts, and preserves exec/env/tags/options; it adds a public executor.ApplyOnce and, like every other candidate, misses lower-layer shortcuts (env/script) wiping scenarios before the merge and execution-segment conflicts.
Compact applyOnceFlag wired into run, cloud run and archive, with a reasonable lib-level ApplyOnce; tests cover run and the unit cases but skip archive and most conflicting flags.
Validates conflicts before consolidation and transforms after it; exported ApplyOnce lives in executor; tests cover the main cases via JSON results and unit tests.

Correct post-consolidation transform with an early conflict check, but it puts a CLI-specific ApplyOnce with '--once' error text into the public lib/executor package; integration and unit tests are solid.

Solid implementation that aggregates multiple conflicting flags into one error and adds a help example; tests are strong (env/tags/scenario name verified at runtime, archive, input not mutated), but the logic sits in public lib/executor and the conflict check is split across two places.

Thorough: conflicts are validated early and multiple conflicts are reported together, help text gets an example, and tests are comprehensive (call order, metric tags, immutability, archive); ApplyOnce still lives in the public lib package.

Kept internal to cmd and detects conflicts from the CLI options layer; the error lists sorted scenario names; unit, integration and archive tests are thorough; the BaseConfig override with a hardcoded type string is slightly roundabout.

Closest in spirit to the reference: cmd-local applyOnce, conflict detection from the parsed CLI options, a sorted scenario-name list in the error, and exit-code assertions, with strong unit, integration and archive tests.
Core logic is fine, but it silently ignores the GetBool error, leaves an unrelated .gitignore '.empryo' entry, and its integration tests are thinner.
Functionally fine with ApplyOnce in lib/executor and reasonable tests, but it adds an unrelated '.empryo' entry to .gitignore and silently discards the GetBool error.
Logic is fine and internal to cmd, but it leaves an unrelated .gitignore edit and adds only unit tests, with no end-to-end run or archive coverage.
Logic is correct, but it includes an unrelated .gitignore change and only adds unit tests, with no run or archive integration coverage.
Correct and well tested, including metrics-tag checks and archive; the logic sits in public lib/executor, and the conflict integration test only checks the message prefix.
Early flag validation and a well-documented ApplyOnce in lib/executor; good integration and archive tests, though the conflict tests only check a generic message prefix.
Thin cmd wrapper over an exported executor.ApplyOnce; tests are extensive, including archive, but it reinvents strings.Count.

Solid wrapper plus lib/executor ApplyOnce with extensive integration, archive and derivation-stability tests; flag is added only to cloud run (not legacy cloud), and a hand-rolled countOccurrences duplicates strings.Count.
Clean internal once.go with separate request and validation helpers; comprehensive tests cover run, scenario tags/env, setup/teardown, each conflict and archive output.

Well-structured cmd-local implementation with a dedicated flag set wired into run, cloud and archive, plus a sentinel error; tests cover run, setup/teardown, env/tags, all conflicting flags and archive, but it misses the lower-layer shortcut drop.
Well-contained cmd/once.go with flag-level unit tests and integration tests for run, tags/env and archive metadata; adds a run help example; the last archive assertion is convoluted.

Self-contained cmd-local implementation that lists scenario names in the error and adds a help example; unit plus integration tests cover the no-op path, exit codes, all conflicts and archive contents (env/tags).
Clean onceRequested plus ApplyOnce in lib/executor; integration tests verify iteration counts with tags and env via JSON output; it shares the gap on lower-layer shortcuts.
Straightforward and correct, with good env/tag preservation checks; the test file name doesn't match the source file, a sumIterations helper duplicates the existing sum, and there is no archive test.
Clean implementation; its integration test that includes startTime confirms extra fields are dropped; no archive test, and the exported API sits in executor.
Early conflict check with an exit code and a clean ApplyOnce; the integration test cleverly verifies that startTime is discarded, but there is no archive test.

Works, but the logic is in config.go while the flag constant is in options.go and the tests are in once_test.go, and it hardcodes the 'shared-iterations' string; tests are reasonable, including archive.

Correct behavior with thorough integration and archive tests, but building a SharedIterationsConfig and then overwriting its BaseConfig is convoluted, and the logic lives in config.go while its tests are in once_test.go.
Introduces an unnecessary new exported error type and DeriveOnceScenarios in executor; tests in existing files cover run and archive adequately.
Works, but it introduces an unnecessary exported OnceScenarioError type in the public lib package; tests across archive, run and unit are adequate.

Slugs are only applied when a page's container dir equals its section base, so pages in non-section subdirectories keep unslugged URLs (fails a hidden test), and the direct treePages lookup is fragile.

Slugs apply to a leaf page only when its container dir equals its section, so pages in nested non-section dirs keep the unslugged path (one hidden test fails); it also reaches into treePages internals with a type assertion.
Correct for typical cases, but it adds a never-used error return and relies on lowercase matching that can break under disablePathToLower with normalized characters.
Works through lowercase prefix matching, but carries the same disablePathToLower normalization weakness plus a never-failing error return and two new descriptor fields.
Prefix map matching works, but its ToLower-based key matching can miss under disablePathToLower when normalization changes more than case (e.g. spaces).
Lowercase-keyed prefix matching works in normal cases but is fragile under disablePathToLower with names needing more than lowercasing.
Path computation is correct, including prefix matching and unnormalized paths, but it overloads ExpandedPermalink to carry the slugged path, which conflates slugs with permalink config.
Correct exact-path matching, but it hijacks ExpandedPermalink (meant for permalink config) to carry slug paths, which is semantically hacky.

Correctly preserves intermediate dirs both between and below sections while touching only page__paths.go, but it routes through the expanded-permalink path, so slugs get QueryUnescaped (e.g. '+' becomes a space).
Routes through the permalink mechanism, and a slug replaces the entire relative segment, swallowing intermediate non-section dirs instead of only the last element.
For regular pages it replaces the whole container dir with the section path, dropping non-section subdirectories (risking URL collisions) and failing a hidden test.
Uses the slugged section path as the leaf container dir, dropping non-section subdirectories, which yields wrong (possibly colliding) URLs (one hidden test fails).
The positional slug replacement is correct, but the patch leaves an unrelated `.empryo` entry in .gitignore.
Depth-indexed slug replacement works, but it adds an unrelated `.empryo` .gitignore entry and its tests mostly assert file existence.
The slug-map approach is correct, but the patch includes an unrelated `.empryo` .gitignore leftover.
A robust exact-path slug map applied in CreateTargetPaths, marred by an unrelated `.empryo` .gitignore change.
Clean slug map applied to section and container dirs; it is correct for nested and intermediate dirs and handles unnormalized paths.
An exact-path slug map applied in CreateTargetPaths is robust to nested non-section dirs and to disablePathToLower; the tests skip nested plain dirs.
Works through a section-chain slug map, but matching normalized Path() against lowercased unnormalized segments is fragile with disablePathToLower and special characters.
Prefix-map matching via strings.ToLower against normalized paths works normally but can mismatch with disablePathToLower when names need normalization beyond lowercasing (e.g. spaces).
Positional replacement via SectionsEntries is correct across deep and intermediate nesting, and the tests cover deep nesting, uglyURLs, and taxonomy/term slugs.
Depth indexing via SectionsEntries is correct and minimal; good tests, including uglyURLs, taxonomy/term and a nested section under a non-section dir.

Adds a path-keyed slug map to the descriptor and applies it to Section.Base and ContainerDir, which keeps non-section intermediate dirs and respects disablePathToLower; it uses an unchecked *pageState type assertion and has no test for non-section subdirectories.
The exact-path slug map approach is correct, but it is inlined with an unchecked `*pageState` type assertion that could panic.
A concise parent walk with positional replacement and cmp.Or fallback that handles intermediate dirs, with thorough tests including deep non-section dirs and taxonomy/term.
Clean depth-indexed replacement walking CurrentSection/Parent, used via cmp.Or; tests cover deep non-section dirs, bundles, taxonomies and auto-created terms.

Positional replacement by section depth correctly handles nested sections and intermediate dirs, with good tests including a non-section subdir; it also edits the docs, which the task did not require.

Depth-indexed slug replacement over the ancestor chain handles nested sections, non-section subdirs, taxonomies, terms and disablePathToLower; the docs edits are relevant but go beyond the task, and the test coverage is solid.

Rebuilds the section dir from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, so a nested section under a non-section directory loses that directory once any slug is present (e.g. /ayuda/deep instead of /ayuda/sub/deep).
Rebuilds the path from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, which drops intermediate non-section dirs between nested sections and breaks such URLs whenever any slug is present.
It returns no slug path for pages whose container dir is not the current section, so those descendants silently keep unslugged URLs and a hidden test fails.
Bails out entirely for leaf pages whose container dir is not the current section, so pages in nested dirs get no slug (one hidden test fails).
Close to the reference, but threads an extra parenPos argument (passing 0 when unused) through applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr; no Pretty update and no validation preservation.
Clean reference-like wrapDurationExpr helper, but it threads an extra parenPos parameter through applyUnaryOp's signature; there is no Pretty fix and no validation preservation.
Minimal fix that wraps the literal and recurses for the unary case; positions use the op rather than the paren, with no Pretty or validation handling.
Minimal, correct wrapping in the paren rule and a recursive wrap in applyUnaryOp that keeps the parse-time out-of-range check; it lacks the Pretty unary-plus fix.
Close to the reference including the Pretty unary-plus fix, and keeps the `(0)` positivity error at the original position; the validation helper covers only the direct paren form.

Wraps the bare literal in a unary-plus Wrapped DurationExpr in both the paren and unary-paren paths and fixes Pretty like the reference; it restores the parse-time `foo[(0)]` check but not `foo[-(5)]`, and the unary path uses the operator position instead of the paren position.
Clean helper with a recursive unary path, and preserves positivity and div/mod-zero validation; Pretty is untouched and no negative tests were added.
Correct wrapping plus recursive constant-value checks for positivity and div/mod by zero; StartPos uses the literal rather than the paren position, and the new validation paths are untested.
Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and changes its String(), then also converts to DurationExpr in some contexts; the dual representation is invasive and convoluted.

Same NumberLiteral.Wrapped AST change plus a printer refactor, new grammar actions including a hand-added generated case, and rewritten DIV/MOD/positive checks; functional but far broader than needed.
Structurally almost identical to the reference wrap helper applied in both paths, plus a useful evaluation-level test; it lacks only the Pretty tweak.
Nearly identical to the reference (a shared wrapDurationExpr helper used by the paren rule and applyUnaryOp) with a nice eval-level test; it misses only the Pretty unary-plus tweak.
Clean minimal fix, but includes an unrelated `.gitignore` debugging leftover.
Simple, correct wrapping, but it carries the unrelated .gitignore `.empryo` artifact and uses literal-based StartPos with no Pretty fix.
Sound minimal fix, but adds an unrelated `.empryo` entry to `.gitignore`.
Correct wrapping in both paths with a retained range check, but it includes an unrelated .gitignore `.empryo` leftover and lacks the Pretty fix.

Wraps the bare literal in a unary-plus Wrapped DurationExpr in both paren paths, keeps parse-time positivity validation, matches the reference Pretty fix, and adds strong tests; the unconditional `$2.(*NumberLiteral)` assertion is slightly fragile.

Correct wrapping with accurate lparen positions, the Pretty fix, and recursive parse-time positivity validation (`(0)`, `-(5)`), backed by thorough parse, printer and eval tests; the unconditional `*NumberLiteral` assertion in the paren rule is slightly brittle.

Works, but also rewrites matrix/subquery/offset handling to set both Range and RangeExpr, reorders subquery printing, and adds an experimental-flag check, creating dual AST state well beyond the issue.

Fixes round-trip but also sets static Range/Step/OriginalOffset alongside the expr fields and flips the printer's Step/StepExpr precedence; these are unrelated behavioural changes with no tests for them.
Clean, minimal wrap helper used in paren_duration_expr and the wrapped unary path; no Pretty update or validation preservation.
Minimal and correct, but its comment wrongly claims the literal was already range-checked, StartPos uses the literal position, and it lacks the Pretty fix.
Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral, changes printing globally, and patches offset_expr and positive_duration_expr; this works but is more invasive than needed.

Adds an exported Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and changes its String(), then layers an unwrapped unary-plus DurationExpr on top; it works but is an invasive AST/API change with a convoluted dual representation.
Correct and keeps positivity and div/mod-zero checks, with good tests including promqltest data; the DurationExpr construction is duplicated inline instead of using a helper.

Correct fix that preserves parse-time positivity and div/mod checks via constantDurationValue, with good parse, error and promqltest eval coverage; the wrapping DurationExpr construction is duplicated inline instead of using a helper.
Correct wrapping in both paths with preserved positivity validation, plus thorough parse, printer and promqltest coverage; no Pretty update.
Wraps with correct lparen positions in both rules and adds a recursive positivity check, with error tests and eval tests; it does not cover div/mod or Pretty.
Correct with validation preserved, but uses a pointer-Item flag parameter, redundant range checks, and churns the generated-file header.
Works and preserves validation and range checks, but uses an `*Item` pointer as a boolean flag and changes the generated-parser header line, an artifact that would fail a regen diff check.
Clean shared helper used in both paren paths and keeps positivity validation via a constant-value helper; Pretty is not updated and tests cover only round-trip and AST updates.
Clean wrapping with lparen positions in both rules and a recursive positivity check, but the added validation has no error tests and there is no Pretty fix.

It traps the wrapped ExecError at walkTemplate and handles `return f a b`, but `try` still swallows return, a bare return in a partial yields nil, and the `return A | B` → `A | B | return` rewrite plus dummy-template node building is over-engineered.
Relies on the ExecError wrapping, so `try` swallows a return; a bare return gives nil, and the creative `return A | B` → `A | B | return` rewrite adds AST complexity the issue wanted removed.

HasValue semantics are right, but return only unwinds as a generic ExecError, so it is not trapped at `template`/`block` boundaries and `try` swallows it; it also edits the forked `parse/node.go`, which hurts fork maintenance.

Passes the existing suite by not touching exec.go, but return travels as a wrapped execution error, so `try` swallows it and returns inside `{{ template }}` end the entire outer template; it also edits the forked parse package.

The executor returns the ReturnError out-of-band with a template-boundary trap, `try` passthrough and HasValue semantics, backed by excellent unit and integration tests; it changes the Executer interface, which is somewhat invasive.

Semantics are correct (HasValue, template trapping, `try`-safe, rendered output on bare return) with good unit and integration tests, but it changes the Executer interface and the executeWithState signature, which is more intrusive to the fork.

There is no template-boundary trap, HasReturn makes any partial with return discard its output even when the return is not hit, and multi-arg wrapping only applies in partials; the texttemplate unit test is a nice touch.
Returns inside a `{{ template }}` call abort the whole template, partials with any return discard their output, and the shorthand wrapping only applies to partials.
Correct HasValue semantics, walkTemplate trap, arg check and arg grouping with good baseof/block tests, but `try` swallows return.
Good HasValue and template-trapping semantics, but `try` swallows the return sentinel, and the tests codify ambiguous non-last-in-pipeline return behavior that the reference rejects.

The recoverReturn wiring is clean and handles `try`, define traps and arg checks, but a partial that contains any return discards its output, so a bare-return guard in a rendering partial returns nothing.

Neat recoverReturn helper with sensible tracking of HasReturn across subtemplates, and `try` is safe; however, a partial containing any return always discards its output and a bare return yields nil, unlike the reference.
Solid sentinel design: HasValue semantics, walkTemplate trap, `try` passthrough, multi-arg wrapping and good tests, marred by an unrelated `.gitignore` leftover.

Clean sentinel with HasValue: a bare return yields the partial's output, valued returns override it, `try` re-panics the sentinel, and template invocations are trapped; it lacks the reference's error checks and adds an unrelated .gitignore entry.

There is no trap at the template boundary, so a return inside `define "main"`/`block` aborts the whole baseof render; a bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the output rendered so far; the `_returnNoop` func and AST-neutralizing pass add complexity the issue wanted removed; it also carries an unrelated `.gitignore` change.
Never traps returns in `{{ template }}` calls; adds a user-visible `_returnNoop` func and an odd neutralizeReturn pass for decorator blocks; a bare return gives nil; includes .gitignore junk.
Similar to C13: correct semantics including `try` and a baseof/block test, but no arg-count check and the namespace move.
Behaviour is close to C6 with good tests and docs; Return silently ignores extra arguments, and `return` again moves to the templates namespace.
Clean implementation with HasValue, walkTemplate trap, `try` passthrough and arg check, plus good tests; moving return to the templates namespace is a reasonable but extra API change.
Solid sentinel, HasValue and trapping design with good tests; moving `return` into the templates namespace (exposing `templates.Return`) is an unrequested API change.
The trap and `try` handling are fine, but removing the arg grouping breaks the documented `return add . 42` form, and a bare return in a partial yields nil.
Drops the `return add . 42` shorthand (no argument wrapping), which regresses existing templates; a bare return gives nil; the trapping and `try` handling are otherwise fine.

It drops support for `return add . 42` (an existing regression); a partial containing any return always returns nil even when the return is not hit, which breaks guard-style early exits; `try` swallows return.
No argument wrapping, so `return add . 42` breaks; `try` is not handled; any partial containing return discards its output, and a bare return gives nil.

There is no walkTemplate trap (a return in `define`/`block` aborts the baseof) and a bare return in a partial yields nil; it rewrites the input of the existing issue-13600 regression test to fit the new pipeline-wrapping behavior.
No trapping in `{{ template }}` calls and a bare return gives nil; it rewrites the whole pipeline into the return value and renames or repurposes the existing issue-13600 regression test.

HasValue semantics are good, walkReturnable in `hugo_template.go` minimizes `exec.go` edits, and the hugolib test is thorough, but `try` is not taught to rethrow return, so `try (return x)` is swallowed.
Good HasValue semantics and a minimal exec.go footprint via walkReturnable, but `try` is not taught to re-panic the sentinel, and the docs add an undefined reference-style link.

The sentinel approach is clean with `try` passthrough, but walkTemplate has no trap, so a return in `define`/`block` kills the outer template, and a bare return in a partial discards the rendered output.
Minimal, but a return inside a `{{ template }}` call aborts the whole outer template, a bare return in a partial gives nil, and there is no argument-count check.
It has a template-boundary trap, `try` handling and an arg check, but it keeps HasReturn so any partial using return (including a bare guard) yields nil when the return is not hit.

Uses a sentinel that walkTemplate traps and that `try` cannot swallow, but it keeps HasReturn, so a partial containing any return discards its output even when the return is not reached, and a bare return gives nil instead of the rendered output; it also edits the generated exec.go directly.
